record.narrative: I audited the new feature_042 panel and the follow-up predictor and interaction screens. The completed feature_042 panel does not support a broad clinically meaningful association across outcomes. H48 is statistically suggestive: signed estimate +0.0440 for outcome_001, just above the approximate 10% threshold of 0.0415, with a 95% interval excluding zero but also extending far below the clinical threshold. Given multiplicity across many feature_042 outcomes and the clinically imprecise lower bound, I keep it unresolved and active rather than accepted. H49, H58, H61, and H62 either have negligible point estimates or intervals that exclude a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction. H59 and H61 include opposite-direction uncertainty but their point estimates are not clinically large, so I close those negative-direction claims. H60 has a wide interval allowing clinical effects, but the point estimate is small and the feature_042 outcome panel is otherwise null, so it is not a priority. The interactions are underpowered: H63 has a large positive point but a very wide interval crossing zero and the clinical threshold; it is useful only as a deferred hypothesis for the main feature_042/outcome_014 signal. H64 is too imprecise to support any interpretation and is closed. The non-feature_042 screens are mostly negative: H40 and H41 are not clinically supported, while H65 remains an active candidate because feature_045 shows a point effect above the small outcome_014 threshold, though statistically imprecise. For validation, H45 is the most scientifically consequential unresolved feature_042 claim: its point estimate is several times the outcome_014 clinical threshold and it is nearly statistically significant. Validating it directly tests whether the lead feature_042 signal extends beyond the already weakly validated H46.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

I therefore register outcome_008/feature_042 in the negative raw direction, as expected if feature_042 marks stronger dependency; a null result would make feature_042 even more outcome-specific. record.narrative:
I audited the new discovery evidence against the approximate 10%-of-absolute-outcome-mean clinical thresholds and the pre-registered claim directions. The main conclusion is that the new feature_045 and feature_054 screens do not reveal a broad clinically meaningful positive association. For feature_045, the outcome_006 positive claim H67 is rejected because the point estimate is in the opposite direction and far below the clinical threshold. The positive outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_004 tests H70, H71, and H72 are not clinically supported: H71 is opposite, while H70 and H72 have point estimates below threshold and confidence intervals that include both no effect and clinically sized uncertainty but do not provide enough evidence to continue as priority leads. For feature_054, the positive outcome_012, outcome_009, and outcome_004 tests H73, H74, and H75 are rejected as unsupported; the estimates are small, imprecise, or opposite. This leaves the earlier outcome_014-only signals as isolated low-threshold leads, but the lower-variance panel fails to corroborate them.

The new feature_042 screens sharpen the feature_042 interpretation. H69, outcome_005, is rejected as a small, statistically non-significant opposite-direction result. H68, outcome_008, is the only statistically significant new result, but its signed estimate is negative while the claim direction is negative: this means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive, not in the claimed direction. Interpreted on the raw scale, the effect is about +0.030 with a positive confidence interval around roughly 0.006 to 0.054. The point is only slightly above the outcome_008 threshold of about 0.028, and the lower bound is far below the clinical threshold. Given that this is a reverse-direction result from a broad outcome screen and not a pre-registered positive claim, I reject H68 as a negative-direction claim and close it; I do not treat the opposite signal as clinically established from these data alone.

H55 is the one new result worth retaining as a low-priority lead. Its point estimate for outcome_014 exceeds the very small threshold of about 0.0093, but the confidence interval is wide and includes zero and clinically meaningful values in both directions. I keep it unresolved and defer further work. The two broad screens H42 and H44 are rejected as unsupported.

For validation, I request independent validation of H48, outcome_001/feature_042. It remains the strongest unresolved pre-registered feature_042 claim: the signed estimate is about +0.044, just above the outcome_001 threshold of about 0.0415, and the interval excludes zero but is clinically imprecise. Validating H48 is more informative than validating the weaker or reverse-direction new screens. If validation replicates with a clinically meaningful magnitude, it would support a dataset-specific association; if not, it would further weaken the feature_042 pattern beyond the already accepted but weakly validated outcome_006 finding H46.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may

record.narrative:
The new validation resolves the due claims and changes the feature_042 story materially. H46, outcome_006/feature_042, remains accepted in the supplied dataset as an associational finding. Discovery R16 is clinically meaningful in the claimed direction: signed estimate +0.0534, with 95% interval +0.0114 to +0.0954, above the approximate 10% threshold of about 0.0175 for outcome_006. Independent validation R27 is directionally consistent but weak: +0.0182, roughly at the clinical threshold, with a wide independent interval -0.0388 to +0.0751. Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The new validations materially weaken confidence in several feature_042/outcome_014 and context-specific leads, while leaving the overall outcome_006/feature_042 association as the only clearly accepted dataset-specific finding. H45 (outcome_014/feature_042, claimed negative association) was directionally consistent in both discovery and validation: signed +0.0351 in discovery and +0.0245 in validation. However, both intervals include zero, and both lower bounds are far below the approximate 0.0093 clinical threshold. Because the outcome_014 threshold is small and the interval is wide, this remains an imprecise secondary lead and I keep it unresolved and deferred rather than reject it outright. H63 (outcome_014/feature_042 interaction within feature_034=1) has a similar pattern: discovery signed +0.0475 and validation signed +0.0343, but the intervals are extremely wide and include zero. It is directionally compatible with stronger effect in feature_034=1, but not enough to support clinically meaningful effect modification; I keep it unresolved and deferred. The most consequential validation is H76, the direct feature_042 association within feature_002=1. Discovery was very strong in this dataset: signed +0.0928 with lower bound +0.0349, above the approximate outcome_006 threshold of about 0.0175. The independent validation is directionally positive but not clinically sized: signed +0.0128, below the clinical threshold, with an interval spanning zero. This does not reverse the discovery estimate, but it prevents H76 from being treated as a robust clinically meaningful subgroup association. record.narrative:
No assessments are due. I therefore use this explore stage to sharpen the current strongest dataset-specific signal and to test a small number of alternative leads. The accepted H46 outcome_006/feature_042 association is accepted only as a narrow dataset-specific association, so the highest-priority question is whether it survives in large complement contexts and whether its apparent concentration in feature_002=1 is robust across other common contexts. I register direct complement estimates within feature_060=0 and feature_034=0; these are not duplicates of H78/H80 and H77/H57, which tested feature_060=1 and feature_034=1. If H46 is a broad dataset association, these complements should remain clinically sized in the claimed negative-dependency direction; if they are null or reversed while feature_002=1 is large, the finding is more likely context-specific, confounded by common population structure, or fragile. I also register feature_042 effects within feature_002=1 stratified by feature_045=0 and feature_045=1. This refines H76/H79/H91 and tests whether the large feature_002=1 signal is genuinely concentrated in one context or merely driven by feature_002 overall. The expected direction is negative; null, opposite, or highly discordant estimates would argue against treating H76 as more than a noisy subgroup lead.

I register a reversal/refinement of H68 for outcome_008. H68 was claimed negative but the returned signed estimate was negative for that direction, implying a raw positive association with point estimate just above the outcome_008 threshold. A direct positive-direction claim is scientifically useful because it is not a new broad feature_042 outcome screen but a follow-up to a near-threshold reverse signal. The main reversal test and a feature_002=1 test ask whether this raw positive association is stable or context-specific.

For outcome_010/feature_006, H21/H11 showed a clinically sized positive raw discovery association but near-null independent validation. I register two direct complements, feature_002=0 and feature_045=0, to determine whether the discovery signal is concentrated in previously tested subgroups or is broadly present but fragile. Broad positive estimates in these large complements would make the lead more credible; null or reversed estimates would support treating it as an unstable or context-dependent lead.

Finally, I register one low-prior but diverse new main-effect screen: feature_037 on lower-variance outcome_012. This is not a high-prior confirmation but it provides a chance to find a new predictor in a lower-variance outcome without reopening the exhausted feature_042/outcome panel. All claims are associational and dataset-specific; acceptance or generalizability would require clinically sized lower bounds and, where useful, independent validation.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, so I make no status changes and select twelve untested analyses. The main goal is to determine whether the accepted dataset-specific outcome_006/feature_042 signal is a broad association or is concentrated in a few contexts and whether the large but validation-fragile feature_002=1 signal is further localized. I run direct complement estimates in feature_002=0, feature_045=0, feature_060=0, and feature_034=0, plus common-context main effects for feature_002 and feature_060 on outcome_006. I also run the joint feature_002/feature_045 strata to see whether feature_045 explains the strong feature_002=1 subgroup signal. These tests directly address concentration versus confounding or instability in the feature_042 evidence. I additionally follow up two secondary signals with large but uncertain evidence: the positive raw outcome_008/feature_042 reversal in feature_002=1, and the direct feature_002=0 and feature_045=0 complements for outcome_010/feature_006, whose near-null validation made concentration or instability the key question. Finally, I include one low-prior new main-effect screen, feature_037 on lower-variance outcome_012, to retain a chance for discovery without reopening the exhausted feature_042 outcome panel. I omit H96 because its evidence is already available from the linked discovery estimate, and defer H84 until the more direct complement and stratification results are seen.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All due results are signed to the registered directions, so positive signed estimates support the claimed negative-dependency or positive-dependency associations depending on direction. Using 10% of absolute outcome mean as the clinical benchmark, outcome_006 threshold is about 0.0175, outcome_008 about 0.0282, outcome_010 about 0.0252, and outcome_012 about 0.0248. The main context tests H88 and H89 on outcome_006 are imprecise: feature_060 is signed +0.0194 with lower bound below zero and feature_002 is signed +0.0209 with lower bound below zero. They are not clinically established, though they are consistent with possible common-context activity and remain low-priority leads. The most important new information is the feature_042/outcome_006 context map. H90 in feature_002=0 is small and broad (signed +0.0085; interval includes clinically sized opposite and positive effects), while earlier H76 in feature_002=1 was large. This contrast supports the idea that the accepted overall H46 association is not uniformly distributed across feature_002 strata; it may be concentrated in feature_002=1 or be confounded with feature_002 structure. H93 in feature_034=0 is the strongest new complement: signed +0.0683 with lower bound +0.0054, so the point estimate is clinically sized and the interval is entirely positive, but the lower bound does not exceed the clinical threshold. This keeps it unresolved and active rather than accepted. H91, H92, and H95 also show clinically sized point estimates in some contexts, but their lower bounds are either below zero or below the threshold; given the large number of context tests, I keep them unresolved and mostly deferred. H94 is the only new direct estimate whose 95% lower bound exceeds the clinical threshold: feature_042 within feature_002=1 and feature_045=0 has signed +0.0974, lower +0.0295. In isolation this is strong discovery evidence for a clinically sized context-specific association in this dataset. However, it is a narrow joint subgroup selected after many feature_042 context analyses, its parent subgroup H76 already had weak independent validation, and the exposed cell is modest. Therefore I do not accept H94 yet; I keep it unresolved active and request independent validation for H94 because that is the most decision-relevant new threshold-clearing signal. For outcome_008, H97 continues the raw positive feature_042 reversal signal in feature_002=1: signed +0.0388, lower +0.0034, above threshold only in point estimate. This is promising but not established, and no validation is spent here because the claim remains imprecise. For outcome_010, H98 shows a clinically sized positive feature_006 association in feature_002=0 (signed +0.0404, lower +0.0045), while H99 is similar in feature_045=0 (signed +0.0419, lower +0.0121). These are interesting complements to the near-null overall validation of feature_006, but their lower bounds do not clear the clinical threshold, so I keep H98 active as the clearer concentration test and defer H99. H100 is a small, near-null new screen on outcome_012 and does not justify follow-up; I reject and close it. Overall, H46 remains the accepted narrow dataset-specific outcome_006/feature_042 association, but the new evidence refines interpretation: it is context-sensitive, possibly concentrated in feature_002=1 and/or feature_034=0, and should not be generalized or treated causally without additional independent evidence.

H48 is a response deadline for outcome_001/feature_042 in the claimed negative-dependency direction. Discovery R29 supported the claim, but independent validation R54 was opposite the claimed direction: the signed estimate was -0.0343 and the 99.6% interval lay mostly on the opposite side of zero. Even if interpreted as raw positive movement, its magnitude is not clearly clinically sized for outcome_001 and it contradicts the original negative-dependency hypothesis. I therefore keep H48 rejected and closed; there is no evidence-based reason to pursue this feature_042/outcome_001 hypothesis further. The key new result is H94. In this supplied dataset, discovery R75 was strong: within feature_002=1 and feature_045=0, feature_042 had signed estimate +0.0974, lower +0.0295, above the approximate outcome_006 clinical threshold of 0.0175. However, independent validation R81 was only +0.0114, below threshold, with a wide interval spanning zero. This is directionally compatible but not clinically supportive. Because H94 was a post-hoc joint subgroup discovered after many feature_042/outcome_006 context tests, and because its parent feature_002=1 context H76 had already failed independent validation, I do not accept H94 as a robust clinically meaningful subgroup association. I keep it unresolved but move it to deferred investigation. This also weakens confidence in treating H76 or other strong feature_042/outcome_006 context estimates as reproducible; I therefore defer H76 as a context lead rather than an active validation priority. The most defensible current conclusion is that H46 remains the only broadly accepted dataset-specific finding: a narrow, associational overall outcome_006/feature_006? correction: feature_042 association, not causally or generally interpretable. Context evidence for feature_042/outcome_006 remains heterogeneous: feature_002=1 and feature_034=0 show large discovery point estimates, but their complements and validations are weaker. The next scientific question is whether the signal is driven by feature_002, feature_045, feature_034, or their intersection. I therefore registered direct joint context tests: feature_002=0 with feature_045=1 to distinguish feature_045-driven from feature_002-driven localization, and feature_002=1 with feature_034=0 to test the intersection suggested by H93 and H76. I also registered feature_002=0 as a complement to the raw positive outcome_008/feature_042 reversal, because H96/H97 remain near threshold but not clinically established. Finally, I registered several low-prior new main-effect screens on lower-variance dependency outcomes to retain diversity without spending validation on imprecise feature_042 contexts.

record.narrative:
No discovery results are due for assessment, so this explore step registers targeted follow-ups of the currently unresolved leads while preserving a small amount of broad exploration. The only accepted finding remains H46: a dataset-specific overall outcome_006/feature_042 association in the negative-dependency direction. Its clinical interpretation is narrowed by context and validation evidence, so the highest-value question is whether a measured biological or technical feature explains the apparent concentration of that association. I register one formal interaction test within a high-feature_018 subgroup, using its median as a tumor-purity-like threshold. The hypothesis is that in higher feature_018 samples the feature_042 raw contrast is more negative, i.e. stronger dependency, than in the complement; because the claim direction is negative, raw negative effect modification should appear as a positive signed interaction. The alternatives are no modification, attenuation, or opposite modification, any of which would argue against treating feature_018 as an interpretable modifier and would keep H46 as a narrow dataset association only.

The second set refines the raw positive outcome_008/feature_042 reversal. H96/H97 are in the positive direction but not clinically established because lower bounds remain below the outcome_008 threshold of about 0.0282. I register direct feature_034=0 and feature_045=0 contexts with a positive-direction claim. If feature_042 has positive raw associations in these broad contexts, the reversal may be more than a feature_002=1 subgroup artifact; if these are null, opposite, or highly discordant, the reversal should be treated as imprecise context noise rather than a candidate effect. The feature_045=0 context is deliberately common enough to avoid overinterpreting very small joint cells.

Third, feature_006/outcome_010 remains unstable: overall raw positive discovery was clinically sized but independent validation was near null. Direct complements feature_034=0 and feature_060=0 test whether the positive association is broad; the joint feature_002=0 and feature_045=0 context tests whether the previously positive complements concentrate in one intersection. Broad positive estimates with lower bounds near or above about 0.0252 would make the lead more credible. Null, opposite, or highly concentrated estimates would support treating feature_006/outcome_010 as a fragile or context-specific lead.

Fourth, feature_001/outcome_001 has a clinically sized raw negative direction in discovery and validation but very imprecise intervals because exposed n is small. I register feature_002=0 and feature_034=0 complements to ask whether the negative-dependency signal is present in a larger stratum or only in an unstable small-cell contrast. These are not validation requests; they are low-cost context refinements of the original H12 lead.

Finally, I register four low-prior main-effect screens on lower-variance outcomes: feature_065/outcome_012, feature_029/outcome_005, feature_052/outcome_016, and feature_011/outcome_007. Their directions are not strongly anticipated; the purpose is diversity and discovery rather than confirmation. Acceptance of any new claim will require a clinically sized point estimate and an interval lower bound supporting the clinical threshold, not just nominal significance. Validation remains reserved for results that clear or nearly clear clinical thresholds and are decision-relevant, not for broad fishing or context estimates whose parent signals have already failed independent validation.

Iteration 8/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
The new results mostly refine context rather than establish clinically meaningful differences. For outcome_006, the feature_018 interaction (H108) is not supportive: signed estimate +0.0071 is below the clinical threshold of about 0.0175 and the interval is broad. Feature_002=0 with feature_045=1 (H102) has a large point estimate, +0.0933, but its lower bound is below zero and exposed n is only 60, so it remains inconclusive and post-hoc. The most promising new result is H103: within feature_002=1 and feature_034=0, feature_042 has signed estimate +0.1054 and 95% lower bound +0.0224, exceeding the outcome_006 clinical threshold. However, this is a narrow joint subgroup selected after many feature_042/outcome_006 context tests, and earlier feature_042 context leads have had weak independent validation. I therefore keep H103 unresolved but active and request independent validation; if validation clears the clinical threshold, this could be accepted as a dataset-specific context association, but without validation it should not be generalized or treated as causal.

The outcome_008 positive-reversal context tests are not clinically established. H109 (+0.0167), H110 (+0.0209), and H101 (+0.0211) all have point estimates below the outcome_008 threshold of about 0.0282 and intervals that include zero or subthreshold effects. These contexts do not support broadening the raw positive feature_042/outcome_008 signal; they remain deferred rather than active leads.

For outcome_010/feature_006, H111 (+0.0276), H112 (+0.0432), and H113 (+0.0538) have some clinically sized point estimates, but their lower bounds remain below the outcome_010 threshold of about 0.0252. Given that the overall feature_006/outcome_010 signal previously had weak independent validation, these context estimates are best treated as fragile or possibly concentrated leads, not accepted associations.

H114 (outcome_001/feature_001 within feature_002=0) has a clinically large point estimate, +0.0901, above the outcome_001 threshold of about 0.0415, but the interval includes zero and exposed n is small. It remains active as a low-confidence context refinement of H12 rather than an established effect.

H116 is a low-prior screen: outcome_012/feature_065 has estimate +0.0169, below the outcome_012 threshold of about 0.0248, with an interval including zero. I keep it unresolved but deferred and do not plan further work unless new evidence raises its priority.

H117 is a clear directional contradiction. Its interval is entirely on the opposite side of zero from the claimed negative-dependency direction, so I reject and close the original claim. Because the evidence may support an opposite association, I registered a reversed refinement of outcome_005/feature_029 in the positive direction for later analysis and possible validation. Validation is requested for H103 because it is the single strongest new candidate: its discovery interval clears the clinical threshold, and independent validation is the decision-relevant test before accepting a post-hoc context association.

record.narrative:
The currently accepted dataset-specific finding remains only H46: an overall outcome_006 association with feature_042 in the negative-dependency direction. The feature_042/outcome_006 context program is not being expanded because feature_002, feature_034, feature_045, feature_060, feature_061, feature_018, and interaction variants have not survived validation or uncertainty checks. The highest-priority new lead is the reversed outcome_005/feature_029 main effect, H120. Its signed estimate is above the approximate 10% relative threshold for outcome_005 (about 0.025), but the 95% lower bound is only 0.0045, so the interval is not clinically informative enough for acceptance. I first register formal interaction tests with the broad binary variables feature_002 and feature_060. For these positive-direction interaction claims, a positive signed interaction means the raw exposed-minus-comparator effect is larger inside the subgroup than in its complement; a null or imprecise interaction supports treating feature_029 as either a broad main effect or a weak context-specific lead, while a negative interaction would argue that the apparent H120 signal is concentrated in the complement. These are falsifiable and directly relevant to deciding whether to validate H120 or a narrow context.

I also register related-outcome screens for feature_029 on outcome_004, outcome_015, and outcome_012. The scientific hypothesis is that feature_029 may mark a broad reduced-dependency state across similar CRISPR dependency outcomes; the alternatives are outcome-specific signal, noise, or no clinically meaningful broad association. Positive raw differences are anticipated on outcome_004 and outcome_015, while outcome_012 is deliberately uncertain because it tests whether the apparent effect generalizes beyond the originally selected outcome. Any acceptance would still require a point estimate above the approximate 0.025 relative threshold and an interval lower bound supporting that threshold, not just nominal significance.

The second follow-up is feature_001/outcome_012. The original feature_001/outcome_001 lead (H12 and its feature_002=0 refinement H114) has clinically large raw negative-dependency point estimates but very wide intervals because exposed n is small. I register the same negative-dependency direction on the lower-variance outcome_012, where a clinically meaningful threshold is about 0.0248 and precision should be better. If feature_001 has a broad negative-dependency association, outcome_012 may sharpen the signal. If it is null or opposite, the outcome_001 lead should remain treated as high-magnitude but unstable.

Finally, I register one outcome_008/feature_042 interaction with feature_002. This is not a revival of the failed feature_042/outcome_006 context program; it targets the distinct positive raw reversal on outcome_008, where H96/H97 had point estimates above the approximate outcome_008 threshold of 0.0282 but lower bounds below it. If the interaction is positive and reasonably precise, the feature_002=1 context could be a candidate for validation. If it is null, opposite, or dominated by uncertainty, the positive reversal should be treated as imprecise context noise rather than a robust association.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
The feature_029/outcome_005 reversal (H120) remains the best current lead, but the new context evidence sharpens rather than confirms it. H120 has signed estimate +0.0324 with 95% lower bound +0.0045: the point estimate exceeds the approximate outcome_005 clinical threshold of +0.0250, but the interval is not clinically informative. H121 (+0.0336, lower -0.0086) and H122 (+0.0317, lower -0.0061) show similar positive associations in feature_002=1 and feature_002=0, and H125's interaction estimate is near zero (+0.0019, lower -0.0544). Thus there is no useful evidence that feature_002 localizes the effect; I keep the subgroup means deferred and the interaction closed. The feature_060 split is more informative for hypothesis generation: feature_060=1 is small and null (H123, +0.0118), whereas feature_060=0 is the largest context estimate (H124, +0.0458, lower +0.0106), still below the clinical lower-bound threshold. H126's formal positive interaction with feature_060=1 is not supported (estimate -0.0339, upper +0.0237 below the threshold), so the positive main effect appears concentrated in the feature_060=0 complement, but that remains an imprecise post-hoc context refinement and I validate the overall H120 claim rather than this subgroup.

The related-outcome screens reduce confidence in a broad reduced-dependency interpretation of feature_029. H127 and H128 are directionally contradicted for positive exposed-minus-comparator effects on outcome_004 and outcome_015, and their intervals do not reach the outcome_005-style clinical threshold. H129 on outcome_012 is near zero, although its interval cannot rule out a positive effect. I therefore keep H129 unresolved but closed, while rejecting H127 and H128. This does not refute an outcome_005-specific association, but it argues against assuming a biologically broad feature_029 effect.

The other new tests are negative for current prioritization. H130 was intended as a lower-variance confirmation of the feature_001 negative-dependency lead, but its signed estimate is opposite the claimed direction (-0.0149) and its upper bound (+0.0185) is below the outcome_012 clinical threshold, so I reject and close it. That weakens the otherwise tantalizing but imprecise feature_001/outcome_001 program. H131 tests localization of the outcome_008 feature_042 positive reversal by feature_002=1; the interaction estimate (+0.0177) is below the outcome_008 clinical threshold and interval-wide, so it does not establish localization. I close it as unresolved rather than rejecting because the upper interval remains above threshold. H105 is a low-prior outcome_005/feature_027 screen with signed estimate opposite/near zero and upper bound far below threshold; reject and close.

I request independent validation for H120. This is the single best scientifically decision-relevant candidate: it is the overall pre-specified reversed main effect, has a clinically sized point estimate and a discovery interval entirely on the positive side, but fails the clinical lower-bound criterion. Validation is a direct test of whether the outcome_005/feature_029 association is robust enough to accept as a dataset-specific association. I deliberately do not validate the narrower feature_060=0 context because it is secondary, post-hoc, and likely underpowered; if H120 validation clears the clinical threshold, I would revisit H124 as a context refinement, and if it does not, the feature_029/outcome_005 program should be closed as not clinically established.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
