Iteration 15/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: The six due results are within-dataset robustness and effect-modification checks for the already accepted H46 association between feature_042=1 versus 0 and outcome_006; they are not independent validation because the validation budget is exhausted. All intervals are signed to the claim direction, so a positive value supports the stated hypothesis of a raw lower outcome_006 score in the exposed group or a stronger exposed-comparator difference in the indicated subgroup. For outcome_006, the absolute-mean scale suggests an approximate 10% anchor near 0.0175. H172 and H173 are simple contrasts in feature_018-low and feature_051-high strata: signed estimates are clinically sized in the expected direction (+0.0479 and +0.0471), but their 95% Welch intervals cross null (-0.0099 to +0.1056; -0.0126 to +0.1068). These are same-direction robustness signals only; they are imprecise and do not justify accepting new subgroup claims. H174 in the feature_051-low stratum is stronger (+0.0599) and its lower bound barely exceeds zero (+0.0005 to +0.1192), but the lower bound is clinically trivial, the interval remains wide, and this is one of many post-specified stratum checks without independent support. I therefore leave it unresolved rather than accept it as a separate context-specific claim. H175 tests whether the contrast is stronger in the feature_051-high stratum; the signed interaction estimate is opposite to the claim (-0.0128) and the interval crosses null, so it fails to support the claimed effect modification. I reject H175 in the operational sense of insufficient support for the stated direction, not as proof that no interaction exists. H84 tests the feature_061-high interaction; the signed point is same direction and above the approximate clinical anchor (+0.0453), but the interval is wide and includes both null and clinically meaningful opposite effects, so it remains inconclusive. H176 duplicates the already assessed feature_060 interaction represented by H80/R63; it adds no new evidence and only confirms an imprecise, null-crossing result, so I close it as reject to prevent double counting. Overall, these checks do not establish that the H46 association is robust across strata or localized to one subgroup. The strongest conclusion supported by this batch is negative or inconclusive: apparent stratum differences are unstable, and the only retained dataset-specific association remains H46, narrowly interpreted as an unadjusted within-dataset association that is not replicated, causal, or generalizable.

All intervals are signed to the claim direction, so a positive value supports the stated hypothesis of a raw lower outcome_006 score in the exposed group or a stronger exposed-comparator difference in the indicated subgroup. For outcome_006, the absolute-mean scale suggests an approximate 10% anchor near 0.0175. H172 and H173 are simple contrasts in feature_018-low and feature_051-high strata: signed estimates are clinically sized in the expected direction (+0.0479 and +0.0471), but their 95% Welch intervals cross null (-0.0099 to +0.1056; -0.0126 to +0.1068). H174 in the feature_051-low stratum is stronger (+0.0599) and its lower bound barely exceeds zero (+0.0005 to +0.1192), but the lower bound is clinically trivial, the interval remains wide, and this is one of many post-specified stratum checks without independent support. I therefore leave it unresolved rather than accept it as a separate context-specific claim. H175 tests whether the contrast is stronger in the feature_051-high stratum; the signed interaction estimate is opposite to the claim (-0.0128) and the interval crosses null, so it fails to support the claimed effect modification. I reject H175 in the operational sense of insufficient support for the stated direction, not as proof that no interaction exists. H84 tests the feature_061-high interaction; the signed point is same direction and above the approximate clinical anchor (+0.0453), but the interval is wide and includes both null and clinically meaningful opposite effects, so it remains inconclusive. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation is exhausted, so the scientifically useful next step is targeted within-dataset discovery using predictors and outcomes that remain largely untested, while continuing to apply a stringent clinical-significance rule. I use an approximate 10% of the absolute outcome mean as the clinical anchor for each outcome, and I will require not only a same-direction point estimate but also an interval lower bound clearly above a clinically meaningful magnitude before treating any new claim as supported. The rare binary predictor feature_032 has not previously been tested; because its positive prevalence is about 5.5%, a positive value may index a minor subtype or state that alters dependency. I hypothesize that feature_032=1 is associated with raw lower dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency, on outcome_012, outcome_008, and outcome_014. The alternative hypothesis is that feature_032=1 marks a resistant or less dependent phenotype, producing raw higher scores, or that it is null. Feature_029 has shown raw lower signals on several other outcomes but has not been assessed against outcome_006, outcome_001, or outcome_008; I extend that pattern to these outcomes and expect raw lower dependency scores in the exposed group, while acknowledging that the prior signal was not independently supported. Feature_048 is an untested categorical predictor with a dominant level_003 group; I compare minority level_001 to level_003 on outcome_005, outcome_012, and outcome_013, predicting that the minority category marks a subtype with stronger dependency. The plausible alternatives are null or reverse direction. Feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 showed several prior estimates in the raw higher direction for outcome_006, outcome_014, and outcome_016, so I test whether that weaker-dependency pattern extends to outcome_008, outcome_001, and outcome_012. The alternative is null or a stronger-dependency effect. These proposals are exploratory, unadjusted comparisons in the supplied dataset only; they do not establish causality, biological identity, clinical utility, or generalizability. If any comparison yields a clinically sized, precise same-direction effect, it will be recorded narrowly as a dataset-specific association and followed only for robustness, not as external validation.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: The new batch is a discovery-only robustness screen on several previously undertested predictors, and none of the due results meets the evidence bar for acceptance. All estimates and intervals are signed to the claim direction, so positive signed values support the stated hypothesis and negative signed values oppose it. I used approximate clinical anchors near 10% of the absolute outcome mean and required a precise, clinically meaningful, direction-consistent result before accepting a new dataset-specific association. Discovery intervals are 95% Welch intervals and were not multiplicity-corrected; this batch also includes correlated outcomes and rare exposures, so I gave extra weight to consistency across related outcomes and cell sizes. H177-H179 tested the rare binary feature_032, with exposed group size only 110. H177 has a signed estimate of -0.0052 on outcome_012, which is opposite to the claimed raw lower-dependency direction and is far below the approximate clinical anchor, with an interval spanning both null directions; reject and close. H178 has a signed estimate of +0.0174 on outcome_008, same direction but below the outcome_008 anchor of roughly 0.028, and the interval is wide and crosses null; this is not a clinically supported association, so reject and close. H179 is the only borderline case: the signed estimate of +0.0685 on outcome_014 is directionally supportive and clinically large relative to the outcome_014 mean, but the 95% interval remains -0.0012 to +0.1381, just including null. With rare exposure, outcome_014 variability, and the inconsistent H177/H178 results, this is best treated as a fragile borderline result rather than an accepted association. I mark it unresolved and deferred because no independent validation is available and within-dataset subgroup mining would increase multiplicity without reducing bias or leakage risk. The feature_029 tests H180-H182 are also unsupported under the stated directions. H180 and H181 have signed negative estimates on outcome_006 and outcome_001, meaning they oppose the claimed raw lower-dependency direction; H180 is also below the outcome_006 anchor, and H181 is well below the outcome_001 anchor. H182 on outcome_008 has a clinically sized signed negative estimate of -0.0336, i.e. evidence for raw higher outcome_008 rather than the claimed raw lower effect, but the signed interval still barely includes null and the due claim direction is not supported. It is not appropriate to flip the claim post hoc without a new registered comparison; and because validation is exhausted, further within-dataset chasing of this opposite signal would be more hypothesis-generating than evidential. Thus H180-H182 reject and close. The feature_048 tests H183-H185 are effectively null or opposite. H183 and H184 have tiny signed negative estimates opposite the claimed direction, with intervals centered on null and well inside clinical triviality. H185 has a supportive signed estimate on outcome_013 of +0.0140, but that is below the approximate anchor of 0.0269 and the interval crosses null. Therefore reject and close. The feature_063 extension tests H186-H188 also fail. H186 on outcome_008 has a small signed negative estimate opposite the claimed raw higher direction. H187 on outcome_001 and H188 on outcome_012 have signed positive estimates of only +0.0074 and +0.0110, respectively, both below their clinical anchors and both with intervals crossing null. These do not support extending earlier feature_063 signals to these outcomes. Overall, this batch adds no new accepted claims. The only supported within-dataset association remains the earlier narrow H46 result for feature_042 and outcome_006, which should still be interpreted only as an unadjusted dataset-specific association because its independent validation was imprecise and the validation budget is now exhausted. record.narrative: Synthesis: no assessments are due, no response-deadline validation is pending, and independent validation capacity is exhausted. The final evidence base supports one narrow within-dataset association: H46. Feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 is associated with a lower outcome_006 CRISPR dependency score. The signed discovery estimate is +0.0534 with a 95% Welch interval of +0.0114 to +0.0954 (R16); because H46 was registered in the lower-outcome direction, this corresponds to an exposed-minus-comparator raw difference of about -0.053. That point estimate is much larger than the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical anchor for outcome_006 (about 0.0175), and the interval excludes the null. However, the interval lower bound does not clear the clinical anchor, and the independent validation estimate R27 was same signed direction but small and imprecise (+0.0181, interval -0.0388 to +0.0751). Therefore H46 should be described as an unadjusted, dataset-specific association with an imprecise clinical magnitude and no reliable independent replication. It is not evidence of causality, biological mechanism, or generalizability. No additional claim meets the scientific bar for acceptance. The initial broad screens for binary and categorical predictors were largely null, and the feature_042 follow-up did not extend robustly to other outcomes. Feature_042 showed a borderline raw higher association with outcome_008 (R42 supporting H96, signed +0.0295, interval +0.0055 to +0.0536), but the lower bound is far below the clinical anchor for outcome_008 (about 0.0282), so I keep it unresolved rather than accepting a dataset-specific effect. The outcome_014 feature_032 signal (H179, R168) is directionally large but the rare exposure and interval that includes null, together with inconsistent H177-H178 results, make it fragile and not acceptable. The feature_006 subgroup and interaction checks for feature_042, including H57, H66, H76, H77-H83, H90-H103, H108-H175 and related interaction contrasts, were unstable: some same-direction subgroup point estimates were clinically large, but validation was attenuated, null, opposite, or imprecise, and no boundary condition was established. Examples include H103 discovery R84 with validation R94 and H94 discovery R75 with validation R81. The final H177-H188 robustness batch also produced no support: rare feature_032 effects were inconsistent, feature_029 tests on outcome_006/001/008 were opposite or insufficiently clinically supported, feature_048 tests were null, and feature_063 extensions on outcome_008/001/012 were too small. Negative or unsupported examples include H45/H63/H163 for feature_042/outcome_014, H48 for feature_042/outcome_001, H11/H21/H117/H120/H141 for other leads, and most early binary screens. The correct conclusion is that most tested predictor-outcome pairs are null or inconclusive under exploratory multiplicity, not that absence is proven. The main unresolved uncertainty is external replication of H46 and the precise effect magnitude. If additional data were available, the most informative next analysis would be a prespecified external independent validation of feature_042=1 versus 0 on outcome_006, with pre-specified unadjusted and covariate-adjusted primary estimation, multiplicity-aware secondary tests for outcome_008 and outcome_014, and no post hoc subgroup mining. Within the supplied dataset alone, further low-priority subgroup searches are not warranted; only a prespecified, high-cell, clinically anchored confirmatory test could be useful, but independent validation cannot be performed in this run.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation is exhausted, so this analyze stage runs the full set of 12 currently registered, active, and untested comparisons: H189-H200. These follow the final exploration plan by testing high-prevalence predictors that have not yet been adequately screened against the most informative outcomes, plus two narrow prespecified interaction follow-ups to the only supported association (feature_042 with outcome_006). The batch is intentionally limited to 12 analyses because each requested comparison can generate new discovery evidence and the analysis budget must be spent on comparisons most likely to clarify whether any additional clinically meaningful predictor-outcome association exists. The primary binary screens are feature_065, feature_021, feature_012, and feature_020 on outcome_006, with claimed raw lower dependency scores; feature_034 on outcome_005, outcome_012, and outcome_015; feature_002 on outcome_005; feature_027 on outcome_001; and feature_060 on outcome_005. I will interpret all returned estimates as signed to the registered direction. For acceptance of a new dataset-specific association, I will require direction consistency, exclusion of the null, and an interval lower bound that clears an approximate 10%-of-absolute-outcome-mean clinical anchor: roughly 0.0175 for outcome_006, 0.025 for outcome_005/012/015, 0.0415 for outcome_001, and 0.028 for outcome_008. Same-direction point estimates that are below anchor or whose intervals remain wide and cross the null will be treated as unresolved or rejected, not accepted. Because these are unadjusted discovery contrasts within a multiplicity-heavy exploration, positive results should be described only as associations in this supplied dataset, with no causal or generalizable interpretation unless externally replicated.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All new comparisons have valid independent-cell Welch evidence, but none satisfies the current acceptance bar for a new dataset-specific association. Estimates are already signed to each claim direction, so positive signed values support the claimed direction and negative signed values oppose it. I used approximate clinical anchors near 10% of the absolute outcome mean and required both clinical meaningfulness and statistical precision; null-crossing intervals were treated as non-support unless there was a very strong, stable, clinically anchored signal. H189, H191, H193, H194, H196, H197, and H198 are small, null-crossing contrasts and were rejected as not supporting the registered claims. record.narrative: No validation response deadline is open, no new validation results arrived, and no voluntary validation request remains. In synthesis I reassess H201 using R179. R179 is signed to the H201 direction and shows a very large positive association of feature_021=1 with outcome_006: signed estimate +0.396, 95% Welch interval +0.325 to +0.467. Because the outcome is scored more negative for stronger dependency, this means feature_021=1 is associated with a substantially higher, weaker-dependency score. The interval excludes the null and is far above the approximate clinical anchor based on 10% of the absolute outcome_006 mean, about 0.0175, so I accept H201 as a precise within-dataset unadjusted association. I close it because independent validation capacity is exhausted. H190 remains rejected as registered; H201 is the properly registered reversal and should not be read as causality, biological mechanism, or generalizability. The other supported within-dataset association remains H46: feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 is associated with lower outcome_006. The signed discovery estimate for H46 is +0.0534, interval +0.0114 to +0.0954, corresponding to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference of about -0.053. Its point estimate exceeds the clinical anchor, but the lower bound does not, and the independent validation R27 was same signed direction but small and imprecise, +0.0181, interval -0.0388 to +0.0751. Thus H46 is an accepted dataset-specific association with clinically uncertain magnitude and weak independent replication. Negative or unsupported evidence is broad: many early and late screens were null or clinically insufficient, including H189, H191, H193, H194, H196, H197, and H198; H192 was opposite to its registered direction but null-crossing; H190 was a precise opposite that motivated H201; feature_006/outcome_010, feature_001/outcome_001, feature_030/outcome_005, feature_029 contrasts, feature_063/054/048/034 extensions, and most feature_042 contrasts outside outcome_006 did not support clinically meaningful new claims after validation or failed validation attenuation. Unresolved uncertainty remains for several signals: H96 feature_042 versus outcome_008 raw higher is statistically positive but its interval starts well below the clinical anchor; H195 feature_034 versus outcome_015 is statistically positive but below or straddling the clinical anchor; H179 feature_032 versus outcome_014 is directionally large but rare and unstable; and H199/H200 are interaction probes with imprecise intervals, now deferred pending direct prespecified subgroup tests H202-H204 if further within-dataset analysis occurs. The most informative next analysis overall is prespecified external replication with covariate adjustment and multiplicity control for the two accepted outcome_006 associations: feature_042=1 associated with lower dependency and feature_021=1 associated with higher weaker-dependency scores. Within the supplied dataset alone, if more analysis is permitted, only the registered high-cell decompositions H202-H204 are worthwhile; they should be judged against clinical-anchor lower bounds, and no additional exploratory subgroup mining should be used to create new claims.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

Iteration 18/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: All eight new discovery comparisons have valid Welch independent-cell evidence and cell sizes above the minimum. I interpreted estimates as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction: positive values support the registered direction, while negative values oppose it. I used pre-specified clinical anchors based on 10% of the absolute outcome mean, approximately 0.0175 for outcome_006, 0.0282 for outcome_008, and 0.0093 for outcome_014, and I treated null-crossing or anchor-inconclusive intervals cautiously because multiple subgroup tests were performed in the same supplied dataset and validation capacity is exhausted.  H202 (outcome_008, feature_042=1 vs 0 within feature_045=1, direction +1) has a clinically meaningful signed point estimate, +0.0529, and the interval excludes zero, so the direction is supported: feature_042=1 is associated with higher, weaker-dependency outcome_008 in this stratum. However, the lower bound +0.0095 is well below the outcome_008 clinical anchor and corresponds to a subthreshold magnitude, while the upper bound is about 0.096. Therefore I accepted neither overclaim nor rejection: the claim is unresolved and deferred because the association is statistically positive but the clinically important magnitude is not established.  H203 (outcome_006, feature_042=1 vs 0 within feature_039 >= 4.9275, direction -1) has signed estimate +0.0772 and interval +0.0189 to +0.1355. The lower bound clears the outcome_006 anchor, so I accept it as a within-dataset association: feature_042=1 is associated with lower, stronger-dependency outcome_006 in the high feature_039 stratum. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Study instructions:

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: Independent validation capacity is exhausted and there are no due assessments, so this explore step registers only targeted within-dataset follow-ups to the strongest accepted signal: feature_021=1 was associated with a markedly higher, weaker-dependency outcome_006 score. The most informative untested registered comparison is H214, the feature_042-by-feature_021 interaction on outcome_006, because it can decide whether the feature_042/outcome_006 association is confined to feature_021=1 carriers. The new proposals are complementary rather than redundant. First, I test whether feature_021=1 versus 0 effect modification differs across a measured continuous prognostic/clinical marker, feature_043, split at its observed median of 5.256. If the raw feature_021 contrast is similar across feature_043 groups, the outcome_006 signal is less dependent on clinical context; if it differs, the association should be described as context-specific. Second, I test feature_021-by-feature_039 interaction because feature_039 high versus low is an accepted boundary condition for the separate feature_042/outcome_006 claim; this asks whether the same molecular stratum also modifies feature_021 effect. Third and fourth, I test feature_021=1 versus 0 on outcome_001 and outcome_013. These are gene-generalization tests: if feature_021 is a broad weak-dependency marker, its positive higher-score contrast should replicate; if it is outcome_006-specific, these should be null or inconsistent. Direction +1 encodes a positive exposed-minus-comparator contrast, i.e. higher outcome score for feature_021=1. For outcome-specific clinical anchoring, I will require the signed point estimate to be at least roughly 10% of the absolute outcome mean and the 95% Welch lower bound to clear that anchor: about 0.0175 for outcome_006, about 0.0415 for outcome_001, and about 0.0269 for outcome_013. Interactions will be accepted as meaningful only if the interaction estimate is clinically anchored and its lower bound clears the same threshold. These comparisons are overlapping unadjusted within-dataset tests, not external validation, causal tests, or generalizability claims.

Iteration 20/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
